uncited: Unlike higher LOD variants that subdivide leaf nodes into smaller blocks, this method treats the entire leaf node as a single cluster, making it distinct from [Medium LOD Approximation](4128-voxel-representation-with-gaussian-lobes.md#medium-lod-approximation) and [High LOD Approximation](4128-voxel-representation-with-gaussian-lobes.md#high-lod-approximation).
The method processes VDB leaf nodes to generate a set of axis-aligned Gaussian primitives.
It distinguishes between dense and sparse leaf nodes to calculate position, opacity, and covariance.
Leaf nodes are either dense (all voxels active) or sparse (subset of voxels active).
*   **Output:** A global array of Gaussian parameters (position, opacity, covariance) and metadata for OptiX Geometry Acceleration Structure (GAS) creation.
The implementation uses thread-local buffers during parallel processing to avoid contention.
*   `thread_gaussian_covariances`: Flat array of diagonal elements of a $3 \times 3$ covariance matrix (variances in X, Y, Z).
Off-diagonal elements are zero (axis-aligned).
**Verify Tiled Storage:** Ensure the VDB grid uses Tiled data storage.
**Parallel Processing:** Process leaf nodes in parallel using Intel Thread Building Blocks (TBB).
*   **Bounding Box:** Traverse all active voxels.
Initialize the bounding box to the dimensions of the starting voxel.
where $\sigma$ and $voxelSize$ are vectors of 3 floating-point values representing radii and voxel dimensions in each axis, respectively.
*   **Tiled Storage:** Essential for correctness.
*   **Precision:** Floating-point precision issues may arise when transforming index coordinates to world space for very large grids.
Choose this when higher fidelity than the single-leaf approximation is needed without the cost of High LOD.
*   **Time Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of leaf nodes, $O(N_{leaves})$.
Sparse nodes require traversal of active voxels, proportional to the number of active voxels in the leaf.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Linear with respect to the number of generated Gaussians.
Not suitable for scenes requiring high-frequency volumetric features.
*   **When to Use:** Low LOD rendering, distant views, or when computational resources are severely constrained.
*   **When Not to Use:** High LOD requirements, close-up views, or when internal density variations within a leaf node are significant.
